name: MAPS
question: Does therapist-led pelvic floor muscle training with indicated bladder training reduce persistent incontinence after radical prostatectomy or TURP compared with standard care?

design.blinding: Participants and therapists unmasked; outcome-data entry blinded

arms.label: Therapist-led pelvic floor muscle training with indicated bladder training

design.population: 853 men with urinary incontinence six weeks after radical prostatectomy (411) or TURP (442) in 34 UK centres.
design.description: Two parallel UK multicentre randomized superiority trials
design.locator: Lancet accepted manuscript pp6–7,10, Table 1; HTA Chapter 2, Study design and populations

verdictNote: Neither trial improved continence; added NHS costs had no QALY advantage.
takeaway: Four one-to-one therapist sessions of pelvic floor muscle training with indicated bladder training did not reduce 12-month incontinence versus standard care after radical prostatectomy or TURP; both UK trials found higher NHS costs without a QALY advantage.

delivery.label: Therapist visits and technique
delivery.value: First 60-minute assessment followed by three approximately 45-minute visits at about 2, 6 and 12 weeks; digital anal examination provided verbal feedback on contractions.
delivery.locator: HTA Chapter 2, Interventions; Chapter 3, Assessment of pelvic floor strength

delivery.label: Home program and urgency treatment
delivery.value: Three maximum-strength contractions with 10-second breaks in lying, sitting and standing, twice daily; sustained contraction during walking and before leakage triggers; urge suppression and bladder training for urgency.
delivery.locator: HTA Chapter 3, Pelvic floor muscle therapy regimen; Bladder training/urge suppression
